---
title: "Demand Forecast"
subtitle: "12-week package demand forecast by region"
---

```{python}
import duckdb
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.graph_objects as go

con = duckdb.connect("../data/warehouse.duckdb", read_only=True)
actuals = con.execute("""
    SELECT region, region_name, period_date, total_packages
    FROM marts.demand_weekly ORDER BY period_date
""").df()

fc = con.execute("""
    SELECT region, model, ds AS period_date, yhat AS packages_forecast
    FROM forecasts.demand_by_region ORDER BY ds
""").df()

metrics = con.execute("""
    SELECT region, model, round(mape, 1) AS mape_pct, round(rmse, 0) AS rmse
    FROM forecasts.demand_by_region_metrics ORDER BY region, model
""").df()
con.close()

regions = sorted(actuals["region"].unique())
```

## Backtest accuracy

Holdout backtest on the last 12 weeks of history (lower is better):

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(metrics.to_markdown(index=False))
```

## Actuals vs forecast by region

::: {.panel-tabset}

```{python}
#| output: asis
# Build one tab per region with a plotly chart each. plotly.js is inlined
# with the first figure so the rendered HTML stays fully self-contained.
# Figure HTML is emitted inside {=html} raw blocks: pandoc passes those
# through verbatim (parsing megabytes of JS as markdown hangs the render).
from plotly.io import to_html

for i, region in enumerate(regions):
    print(f"\n### {region}\n")
    a = actuals[actuals["region"] == region]
    f = fc[fc["region"] == region]

    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_scatter(
        x=a["period_date"], y=a["total_packages"],
        mode="lines", name="Actual",
    )
    for model, mf in f.groupby("model"):
        fig.add_scatter(
            x=mf["period_date"], y=mf["packages_forecast"],
            mode="lines", line=dict(dash="dot"), name=f"Forecast ({model})",
        )
    fig.update_layout(
        height=420, legend_title=None,
        xaxis_title="Week", yaxis_title="Packages",
    )
    fig_html = to_html(
        fig, include_plotlyjs="inline" if i == 0 else False, full_html=False
    )
    print("```{=html}\n" + fig_html + "\n```")
```

:::
